title: Mixed storage workloads
purpose: Measure sequential and 4K random read and write throughput at realistic queue depths, tail latency, and fsync durability cost, against a regular file opened with direct I/O so the result describes the device rather than the page cache.

implementation.note: Native rather than an fio adapter. fio's methodology is followed (direct=1, warm-up before recording, realistic queue depths) but not its binary: the product requires a single static binary that runs anywhere it is copied, and a storage module that only worked where fio happened to be installed would leave the Storage category empty on most hosts. An fio adapter remains worthwhile later as a cross-check and as a route to io_uring queue depths.

safety.note: The path is composed by the agent's StatePath and the module appends one compile-time constant name. O_NOFOLLOW means a symlink planted at that path cannot redirect the open at a block device, O_EXCL means a link that reappears after the stale-fixture removal aborts creation instead of being written through, and the open file is asserted to be a regular file before any byte is written. Never a raw block device, ever, by any flag.

sizing.note: The fixture is the smaller of the preferred size and a fraction of free space, rounded down to whole large blocks. Unknown free space yields the minimum and the run is refused, never treated as unlimited.

preparation: Remove any fixture left by a crashed run, create the file exclusively, fill it with non-zero data so it is fully allocated rather than sparse, and fsync it before measuring. A sparse file would let reads be answered from a hole without the device being touched.
calibration: Per workload, grow a probe from one operation by a bounded proportional step until a repetition exceeds a quarter of target_rep_ms, then extrapolate linearly. Capped at 2^24 operations.
warmup: warmup_reps repetitions per metric, streamed and retained but excluded from statistics.

workloads.description: 1 MiB blocks read in order, one outstanding operation.
workloads.represents: Streaming a large file: backups, media, log shipping

workloads.description: 1 MiB blocks written in order, one outstanding operation.
4 KiB reads at random block-aligned offsets, one outstanding operation.
workloads.represents: An index probe with nothing to overlap it

workloads.description: The same, with sixteen operations outstanding.
workloads.represents: A busy server with many requests in flight

workloads.description: 4 KiB writes at random block-aligned offsets, one outstanding operation.
The same, with sixteen operations outstanding.
70% reads, 30% writes, 4 KiB, sixteen outstanding. Different from running the two separately because a device's read and write paths contend.
99th percentile of per-operation read latency, by nearest rank, captured from the QD1 random read repetitions.
workloads.represents: The slow 1% of reads, which is what a user notices

workloads.description: 99th percentile of per-operation write latency, captured from the QD1 random write repetitions.
One 4 KiB write followed by fsync of the data, per operation.
workloads.represents: What every database commit pays for durability

shapes.measures: device response time with nothing to overlap it

shapes.note: Reached with one thread per outstanding operation, fio's numjobs model rather than its iodepth model: without io_uring or libaio, which are not reachable from safe Rust, concurrent threads are how a device is given more than one request. Depth 16 rather than a vanity 256, because a web server does not run 256 outstanding I/Os.

derived_metrics.formula: median(last third of measured reps) / median(first third)
derived_metrics.note: Reported per write workload. Below 0.70 the run visibly slowed as it went, which is the shape of an SLC cache filling up, a burst allowance running out or a thermal limit. Published rather than averaged away, because the opening figure is then not the device's sustained speed.

validation: Every workload must produce at least 5 measured repetitions.
Repetitions shorter than 20 ms are rejected as timer-noise dominated.
A filesystem that refuses direct I/O downgrades the result: the figures then describe the page cache as well as the device.
Throughput falling below 70% of its opening level across the repetitions is reported as a steady-state failure, not averaged away.
A percentile is withheld when any repetition completed fewer than 100 operations, because a p99 from a handful of observations is a number wearing a statistical name.
Coefficient of variation above 0.20 raises a high-variance warning and downgrades the result to Degraded.
abort_conditions: the fixture does not fit in the free space reported
cleanup: The single fixture file is removed when the module returns, on every exit path including errors and cancellation, and a fixture left behind by a crashed run is removed before a new one is created.
limitations: Measures the filesystem and the storage stack as configured, not the bare device: RAID, LVM, ZFS, virtio and the mount options all sit in the path and are recorded in the environment snapshot for that reason.
Queue depth is reached with one thread per outstanding operation rather than an asynchronous submission queue, so a small amount of scheduling overhead is charged to the result at depth 16.

No SSD preconditioning is performed. A drive that has been idle will report its burst behaviour in the first repetitions; the steady-state ratio is published so that is visible rather than hidden, but a full preconditioning pass would take hours and write far more than a benchmark should.
The fixture is a fraction of free space, so a nearly-full disk is measured over a smaller offset range than an empty one. The size used is recorded.

fsync latency depends on whether the device or its controller honours cache flushes. A drive that lies about flushing will report an excellent number here, and no benchmark run from userspace can detect that.

scoring.note: Random I/O and durability outweigh streaming, because a web server almost never streams a whole file but pays fsync on every write its database commits. Reference anchors are declared targets, not measurements. See docs/SCORING-SYSTEM.md.
